core_obligations: Reduce to the case of a stack over the spectrum of an algebraically closed field by base change along the given point, noting that being in the image only gives a lift after a field extension and that one may pass to the reduction (proof lines 2986-2996)

Choose a field-valued surjective flat cover of the now nonempty stack and use the diagonal characterization of universal injectivity to make the morphism comparing the two projections of the square of that cover surjective (proof lines 2997-3002)

Compare the two projections: over an algebraically closed field the tensor square of the field is a domain, so a point of the fibre product over the generic point exists, and its component is an integral scheme on which the two images of the field have equal integral closures (proof lines 3003-3016)

Conclude: reading the equality of integral closures in the residue field of that point shows that the field extension is trivial, so the cover is a point of the stack over the original field (proof lines 3017-3029)
proof_roadmap: 先沿 y 作基变换，化为「非空的 X 一致单射地映到 Spec(k)」，要找 k-点；可设 X 既约。
取域 k' 与满平坦局部有限型覆盖 Spec(k') → X；一致单射 ⇒ Spec(k') ×_X Spec(k') → Spec(k' ⊗_k k') 满。
k 代数闭 ⇒ k' ⊗_k k' 是整环；取其泛点所在连通分支的既约闭子概型 U，两支投影局部有限型。
由 Varieties 的「两像的整闭包相等」命题，在 κ(ξ) 里 λ ⊗ 1 代数依赖于 1 ⊗ k'；k 代数闭 ⇒ k' = k。
difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that for a universally injective morphism of algebraic stacks and a point of the target over an algebraically closed field which lies in the image on spaces, there is a point of the source over that same field mapping to it (author lemma at source lines 2976-2984, label lemma-universally-injective-point). The proof (source lines 2986-3030) reduces by base change to a nonempty stack over an algebraically closed field, takes a field-valued flat surjective cover, uses the diagonal characterization of universal injectivity to get surjectivity of the comparison morphism, and then compares the two projections through the integral closure statement to force the field extension to be trivial. H3; the reduction is not the content, the comparison of the two projections and the closing field-theoretic argument (proof lines 3003-3029) are.
